analysis: Increasing training negatives from 16 to 64 reduced macro validation HR@10 from 0.4713 to 0.4462, a decline of 0.0251. The result also remained below the reported SASRec baseline of 0.505. Category HR@10 was 0.470 Movies_and_TV, 0.500 Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.335 Electronics, and 0.480 CDs_and_Vinyl. This controlled trial does not support the hypothesis that insufficient negative competition was limiting performance. More negatives changed the sampled classification objective and computation, but the available results do not establish why performance declined; convergence, checkpoint timing, and optimization effects remain unverified. Retain 16 negatives as the stronger observed configuration.
code_summary: AttentiveSimilarity uses separate 96-dimensional context and target item embeddings, learned item biases, and candidate-conditioned attention through 32-dimensional projections. Scores aggregate history–candidate dot products using bounded exponential attention and square-root attention-mass normalization. Training reconstructs an arbitrary observed item from its remaining history, with mixed recent/random truncation to 128 items and 15% context dropout. This trial changed only NEGATIVES from 16 to 64: each example contains one positive followed by 64 uniformly sampled negatives, excluding the full training history while allowing duplicate negatives. Cross-entropy, embedding regularization, AdamW, checkpoint selection, stopping limits, all four dataset routes, and the architecture-loading predictor writer were preserved. Host execution succeeded and independent validation produced macro HR@10 of 0.4462.
